skill.name: remotion-render
skill.description: Render React and Remotion TSX components as videos through the inference.sh cloud service. Configure dimensions, frame rate, duration, codec, props, and composition ID.
skill.summary: Submit Remotion TSX and receive a rendered video with configurable output settings.
skill.author: 101-skills

security_audit.summary: Eight findings confirm commands that authenticate, submit rendering jobs, or install remote skill packages. One network finding confirms a remote image request; remaining matches are Markdown syntax, source examples, or documentation links. The workflows also send TSX and props to inference.sh for cloud execution.

remediation.issue: The instructions install remote skill packages with npx.
remediation.suggestion: Pin package versions and advise users to review package provenance before installation.

remediation.issue: The skill embeds an image from a third-party cloud URL.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle the image locally or serve it through a trusted marketplace proxy.

remediation.issue: Render requests transmit TSX, props, and settings to a cloud service.
remediation.suggestion: Disclose this transfer before execution and warn users not to submit secrets or proprietary code.

content.value_statement: Turning React animation code into shareable video requires a configured rendering pipeline. This skill submits Remotion TSX to inference.sh and returns rendered video output.
actual_capabilities: Submits default-exported React and Remotion TSX components for cloud rendering.
Configures video width, height, frame rate, duration, and codec.
Passes structured props into rendered components.
Uses Remotion animation APIs such as spring, interpolate, Sequence, Audio, Video, and Img.
Supports CLI rendering through belt and Python SDK rendering through inferencesh.
Streams render progress and returns the resulting video location.
limitations: Requires an inference.sh account, belt authentication, and network access.
Sends component code, props, and render settings to an external cloud service.
Only React and Remotion imports are documented as available.
Does not document local rendering, editing, hosting, or long-term output retention.

use_cases.title: Create Product Motion Graphics
use_cases.description: Render branded titles, counters, and transitions from reusable React components.

use_cases.title: Generate Data-Driven Videos
use_cases.description: Pass changing values through props to produce repeatable reports or social clips.

use_cases.title: Prototype Remotion Animations
use_cases.description: Test timing, interpolation, sequences, and spring motion without configuring a local renderer.

prompt_templates.title: Render Simple Text
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a three-second Remotion video showing [text] fading onto a [background color] background. Render at [width] by [height] and [fps] FPS.

prompt_templates.title: Animate Provided Data
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a Remotion counter using [data values] and [brand colors]. Pass the values as props and render a [duration]-second video.

prompt_templates.title: Sequence a Branded Clip
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Remotion composition with [scene count] timed scenes, [transition style], and [media assets]. Use the supplied brand rules and render settings.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Parameterized Video System
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a reusable Remotion component for [campaign]. Validate [input fields], sequence [content stages], stream render progress, and produce variants for [formats].

output_examples.input: Render a square loading counter from zero to one hundred over five seconds.
output_examples.output: A 1080 by 1080 video with a centered percentage counter, dark background, 60 FPS timing, and the returned video location.

output_examples.input: Create a three-scene product announcement using supplied titles and brand colors.
output: A reusable Remotion composition with timed scenes and fade transitions.
Props for titles, subtitles, and colors.
A rendered video location after cloud processing.

output_examples.input: Render a logo entrance using spring motion.
output_examples.output: A two-second video where the logo scales smoothly into view using configured spring damping and stiffness.

best_practices: Keep component inputs explicit and pass changing content through props.
Choose frame rate, duration, and dimensions before tuning animation timing.
Review code and remove secrets before submitting any cloud render request.
anti_patterns: Do not include credentials, private URLs, or confidential data in TSX or props.
Do not install unpinned remote skills without reviewing their source and publisher.
Do not assume remote assets or unsupported packages are available during rendering.

faq.question: What input does the renderer require?
faq.answer: It requires TSX code that default-exports a React component. Other render settings are optional.

faq.question: Which animation APIs can I use?
faq.answer: The documentation lists React and common Remotion APIs, including spring, interpolate, Sequence, Audio, Video, and Img.

faq.question: Can I pass dynamic content?
faq.answer: Yes. Supply a props object and receive those values in the exported component.

faq.question: Does rendering happen locally?
faq.answer: No. The examples submit code and settings to the inference.sh cloud application.

faq.question: What setup is required?
faq.answer: Install the belt CLI or Python SDK, authenticate with inference.sh, and maintain network access.

faq.question: Can I monitor a long render?
faq.answer: Yes. The Python SDK example streams progress updates and reports the video location when available.
